issue.title: Delete the remote-attention per-revision legacy migration once no host holds legacy rows

task_type_fields.proposal:
Proposed by phase sase-1tz.4.1.3 (attention_key) note #3; filed by the sase-1tz.4.1 land agent.

Delete the one-time remote-attention legacy migration once no host still holds an
undismissed per-revision row. In `src/sase/dispatch/attention_inbox.py` that means:
- the supersede/fold branch in `reconcile_remote_attention_inbox`, commented at about
  line 215 as removable once no host has legacy rows;
- `_legacy_rows_by_identity`;
- `_inherit_legacy_browsing_state`;
- their tests in `tests/test_dispatch_attention_inbox_legacy.py`.

Gate: after the human installs the epic, the first TUI refresh dismisses every
per-revision row for a pending request with the reversible marker, and compaction
archives those rows 3 days later. Before deleting anything, run the jq census recorded
on sase-1tz.4.1.3 note #1 on athena and apollo (`ssh apollo`). It must show 0 live
remote-attention rows whose `dedup_key` has 4 colon-separated fields
(`remote-attention:{origin}:{request_id}:{revision}`).
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Epic sase-1tz.4.1 had to ship the migration and could not remove it: removal depends on
post-install live state on athena and apollo, and the epic treated live hosts as
read-only with install left to the human. The code is harmless meanwhile, because it is
a no-op once no legacy rows remain.

issue.creation_reason: The sase-1tz.4.1 attention_key phase shipped a one-time legacy-row migration that can only be removed after install, once a live census shows no per-revision rows remain.
